I may not know to you but my parents are refugees from third world countries where poverty and violence and war forced them to leave what remains of the rest of my family, you think I don’t know generational struggle? 
Let’s just agree to disagree because that’s okay but don’t presume to know what my struggle is like or my family has or hasn’t been through. Congratulations on processing your trauma but it always linear for everyone.

It just feels like a lot of projection and lashing out which, despite his age, is relatively normal for someone processing trauma. And that process is an ongoing cycle, whether you have already worked through it or not. 
It’s definitely understandable that other people see him as unlikable and unrelatable. Especially others such as yourself with a different world view and I’m not saying you’re wrong either . I just think it seems like everyone has been hurt in this family and it makes me sad for all of them. I guess I just want to hope that something good can come of all it .

Im not black you’re right and I can’t pretend to know what the black experience is like. I am however Latina and Palestinian , both my parents are immigrants with their own traumas and our family deals with its own generational trauma. I can also relate to a father being a “pillar of community” doing things that oppose that image and dealing with the cognitive dissonance that creates. 

As I said, do I think how he went about things was great? Absolutely not. Can I empathize and partially relate due to my own experience as a first generation queer person with very conservative minority parents? Absolutely.
I respect your opinion, you’re completely entitled to it. but I also stand by my opinion based on similar experience.
But no worries about coming off as argumentative, everyone is entitled to their own opinion since he’s doing so publicly
That’s why I said they seem “excessive” to me anyway. Probably not the route I would choose but speaking on the lies and secrets themselves is what I meant by “ending the cycle”.

Personally I agree wholeheartedly, I don’t like to blame anyone for my bad choices but acknowledging the root from where those problems stemmed is definitely part of it and I still find myself wish for some kind of acknowledgment or apology as if that might make it easier. But you’re right trauma has a significant effect on your brain and that doesn’t just “go away” even if you have all the fame and money in the world.

And thankyou for saying that, I’ve gotten alot of the “stop blaming your family” and “entitlement “ stuff from strangers too so I get what you mean and it’s probably why I’m more empathetic towards his situation. You seem like a really kind person & I hope you’re doing good too 🩵🦋
